measures.short_title: Lieutenant governor vacancies and legislative officer pay
measures.summary: Provides an election to fill a lieutenant governor vacancy early in a term, lets the Legislature set pay for the lieutenant governor and legislative officers by joint resolution, and requires a legislative officer to approve legislative travel spending.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Sen. Sam Givhan R; passed both chambers unanimously; no organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Process for merging county school systems
measures.summary: Creates a constitutional process for merging neighboring county school systems, with a State Board of Education impact study and a protest and referendum procedure.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Rep. Terri Collins R; passed House 96 to 2 and Senate unanimously; no organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Daily Pledge and student led prayer in schools
measures.summary: Requires local school boards to adopt policies for a daily Pledge of Allegiance in public K to 12 schools and authorizes policies allowing student initiated, student led prayer.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Rep. Reed Ingram R; passed House 94 to 4 and Senate unanimously; no organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Weekly national anthem in public schools
measures.summary: Requires local school boards to adopt policies for each public K to 12 school to play or perform the first stanza of the Star Spangled Banner at least once a week.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Sen. Gerald Allen R; passed Senate 22 to 5 and House 75 to 27; no organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Only U.S. citizens may vote
measures.summary: Amends the constitution so only U.S. citizens who meet state qualifications may vote in state and local elections in Arkansas.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; critics cited by the UA Public Policy Center say it could lead to stricter proof of citizenship rules; no campaign money reported.

polls.note: SMS text to web; MOE +/-4.7

measures.short_title: Right to bear arms shall not be infringed
measures.summary: Declares the right to keep and bear arms, including ammunition, accessories and components, a natural, fundamental and individual right that shall not be infringed.
measures.campaign: Supporters say it clarifies what arms covers; opponents worry the without limitation wording could conflict with bans on gun possession by felons or domestic abusers; no money reported.

polls.note: SMS text to web; MOE +/-4.7

measures.short_title: Economic development districts and public loans
measures.summary: Lets the General Assembly create economic development districts and fund programs, loans and grants of public money, including district bonds for industrial, headquarters or sports projects.
measures.campaign: No organized support or opposition or money reported.

polls.note: SMS text to web; MOE +/-4.7

measures.short_title: $500 million water infrastructure bonds
measures.summary: Authorizes the Arkansas Natural Resources Commission to issue up to $500 million in general obligation bonds for water, waste disposal, pollution control, flood control, irrigation and wetlands projects.
measures.campaign: Legislatively referred bond issue; no organized opposition or money reported.

polls.note: SMS text to web; MOE +/-4.7

measures.short_title: Bigger rainy day fund with required deposits
measures.summary: Raises the Budget Stabilization Fund cap to 25% of general revenue and requires annual transfers of $750 million until the cap is met, with limited suspension and withdrawal rules.
measures.threshold_note: Florida constitutional amendments need 60% of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Republican Party of Florida endorses; Jolly D supports with guardrails; Gov. DeSantis calls it foolish and Donalds R opposes; Miami-Dade and Palm Beach Democratic parties urge no; no money reported.

measures.short_title: Property tax exemption for farm equipment
measures.summary: Exempts tangible personal property such as farm equipment used for agricultural production or agritourism on agricultural land from property taxes starting in 2027.
measures.threshold_note: Florida constitutional amendments need 60% of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Sen. Keith Truenow R; Hillsborough County Democratic Party opposes; about $31M a year local revenue loss estimated; no money reported.

measures.short_title: Large homestead property tax cut toward elimination
measures.summary: Exempts the first $250,000 of homestead value from non school levies on a schedule toward full elimination, limits local property tax uses and future business assessments, and requires five years residency for new residents to get the larger exemption.
measures.threshold_note: Florida constitutional amendments need 60% of votes cast on the measure. Placed by HJR 1F.
measures.campaign: Yes on 3 backed by RPOF, Gov. DeSantis and Florida Realtors, which has spent about $18M; opposed by the Florida Democratic Party, many local officials, sheriffs and public employee unions; Florida Policy Institute estimates $12B recurring local revenue loss.

polls.note: Population reported only as Florida voters; sponsor not stated; no undecided reported, appears forced choice; MOE +/-3.8

measures.short_title: Raise conservation use acreage cap to 4,000
measures.summary: Doubles the maximum acreage that can qualify for bona fide conservation use property tax assessment from 2,000 to 4,000 acres.
measures.campaign: HR 32 2025; passed with two thirds; no organized campaign or polling reported.

measures.short_title: Nonpartisan elections for all probate judges
measures.summary: Requires all probate court judges to be elected in nonpartisan elections.
measures.campaign: HR 251; no organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Dedicated Next Generation 911 fund
measures.summary: Authorizes the General Assembly to dedicate existing revenues, such as 911 fees, to a nonlapsing fund used only for 911 systems.
measures.campaign: HR 1243 per the SOS booklet, News4JAX lists HR 1251; no organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Limit governor pardons near gubernatorial election
measures.summary: Bars the governor from granting pardons, commutations or reprieves from 60 days before the gubernatorial election until the new term begins, except in impeachment matters.
measures.campaign: SB 10 by Sen. Chris McDaniel R, prompted by Gov. Bevin's 2019 end of term pardons; no organized opposition or money reported. Ballot question says the window ends at swearing in while the text says the fifth Tuesday after the election.

measures.short_title: Surviving spouse can transfer disabled veteran exemption
measures.summary: Lets a surviving spouse of a qualifying disabled veteran move the homestead property tax exemption to a new home one time.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Keep right to restore prior maximum millage
measures.summary: Lets local taxing authorities levy below their prior maximum rate without permanently losing the ability to return to a previously authorized maximum, up to the voter approved cap.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: No post conviction bail for crimes against minors
measures.summary: Prohibits post conviction bail for people convicted of certain aggravated offenses against children.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Lifetime two term limit for governor
measures.summary: Bars anyone who has served more than one and a half terms as governor from being elected again, making two terms a lifetime limit.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Reps. Mike Bayham R and Mandie Landry D; no organized campaign or money reported.

measures.short_title: Flexibility in paying retirement system debt
measures.summary: Removes the rule that nonrecurring state money must pay a retirement system's oldest unfunded liability first.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Extra local property tax exemption for seniors
measures.summary: Lets parishes and municipalities offer an additional homestead exemption of up to $30,000 assessed value, rising with age, to qualifying homeowners 65 and older.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Public funds for private drinking water lines
measures.summary: Allows public funds to identify, remove or replace hazardous drinking water service lines on customer owned property.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Bar foreign adversaries from expropriating property
measures.summary: Prohibits foreign adversaries and their agents from using expropriation to acquire private property.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Raise income limit for assessment freeze to $150,000
measures.summary: Raises the income limit for the special property tax assessment level freeze from $100,000 to $150,000.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.short_title: Tax exemption for rehabilitated blighted property
measures.summary: Lets parishes create property tax exemptions for rehabilitated blighted or abandoned property.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral; no organized campaign, money or polling reported; PAR Louisiana guide summarizes arguments.

measures.id: Constitutional Amendment - Require Photo ID for Voting
measures.short_title: Photo ID for all voters including mail
measures.summary: Requires every voter, not only those voting in person, to present photo identification before voting.
measures.campaign: Backed by Republican legislative majority; opposed by Democrats and voting rights groups; no money reported.

measures.id: Constitutional Amendment - Maximum Income Tax Rate of 3.5%
measures.short_title: Cap state income tax rate at 3.5%
measures.summary: Lowers the constitutional cap on the state income tax rate from 7% to 3.5%.
measures.campaign: Backed by Republican legislators; NC groups launched a campaign to defeat the two tax amendments; no money reported.

polls.note: YouGov online; 1,121 adults matched to 800, LV subsample size not reported; MOE +/-5.5 LV; ballot text wording

polls.sponsor: Catawba College Center for NC Politics & Public Service
polls.note: Fielded August 2026, exact dates not given; released 2026-09-02; only support reported; with arguments on both sides support was 66

measures.id: Constitutional Amendment - Property Tax Levy Limit
measures.short_title: Require limits on local property tax increases
measures.summary: Requires the General Assembly to enact limits on how much local governments can raise property taxes.
measures.campaign: Backed by Republican legislators incl. Senate Leader Berger; local government advocates and Democrats warn of service cuts; targeted by the campaign against the two tax amendments.

polls.note: YouGov online; 1,121 adults matched to 800, LV subsample size not reported; MOE +/-5.5 LV; ballot text wording

polls.sponsor: Catawba College Center for NC Politics & Public Service

measures.short_title: Restructure Judicial Nominating Commission
measures.summary: Changes who can serve on the Judicial Nominating Commission and how members are selected, including appointments by current congressional districts.
measures.campaign: Legislative referral from the GOP majority; Oklahoma Policy Institute urges no, saying it strips protections in choosing top judges; no money reported.

measures.short_title: Lower annual caps on taxable property value growth
measures.summary: Lowers annual caps on growth in taxable value from 3% to 1.75% for homesteads and farmland and from 5% to 4% for other property, and replaces the senior freeze with income based caps, starting 2027.
measures.campaign: Authored by House Speaker Kyle Hilbert R, backed by Oklahoma Farm Bureau; opposed by Oklahoma Policy Institute and some Democrats over school and local revenue.

measures.short_title: Remove right to bail for specified serious offenses
measures.summary: Removes the constitutional right to bail for defendants charged with specified serious felonies when proof is evident, letting judges deny pretrial release.
measures.threshold_note: Must receive a majority of all votes cast in the governor's race, not just a majority of votes on the amendment.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by House Speaker Cameron Sexton R; Tennessee Association of Professional Bail Agents organizing opposition; no money reported.

measures.short_title: Ban a state property tax
measures.summary: Prohibits the legislature from enacting taxes on property.
measures.threshold_note: Must receive a majority of all votes cast in the governor's race, not just a majority of votes on the amendment.
measures.campaign: Yes on 2 campaign launched by Republican leaders with the Tennessee Chamber and Farm Bureau; no organized opposition reported.

measures.short_title: Marsy's Law crime victims' rights
measures.summary: Rewrites and expands the constitutional list of crime victims' rights, including notice, being heard, restitution and a speedy trial.
measures.threshold_note: Must receive a majority of all votes cast in the governor's race, not just a majority of votes on the amendment.
measures.campaign: No visible campaign; some question cost implications.

measures.short_title: Right to reproductive freedom including abortion
measures.summary: Adds a constitutional right to make one's own decisions about pregnancy, contraception, abortion and fertility care, allowing third trimester restrictions with health exceptions.
measures.campaign: Supported by Gov. Spanberger, ACLU of Virginia, Planned Parenthood Virginia, Reproductive Freedom for All; opposed by Winsome Earle-Sears' vote no tour, Virginia Catholic Conference, Family Foundation; money not found.

polls.note: Wason Center CNU; asked before final legislative passage, describing the amendment generally; only support/strongly support published; MOE +/-4.4

measures.short_title: Repeal same sex marriage ban
measures.summary: Removes the 2006 ban on same sex marriage and affirms that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender or race with equal legal treatment.
measures.campaign: Supported by Gov. Spanberger and Democratic legislators; opposed by Earle-Sears and conservative groups; money not found.

measures.short_title: Automatic voting rights restoration after prison
measures.summary: Establishes a fundamental right to vote and automatically restores voting rights to people with felony convictions upon release from incarceration, and replaces the mental incompetence bar with a capacity standard.
measures.campaign: Democratic referral; Republican opposition; no committee money found.

polls.note: Wason Center CNU; asked before final legislative passage, describing the amendment generally; only support/strongly support published; MOE +/-4.4

measures.short_title: Only U.S. citizens may vote
measures.summary: Adds a requirement to the constitution that only U.S. citizens who are West Virginia residents may vote, barring local noncitizen voting.
measures.campaign: SJR 9 passed unanimously; Americans for Citizen Voting supports; League of Women Voters of WV and WV Citizen Action Group oppose; no money reported.
